name: Manasseh
overview: Manasseh was a male member of the tribe of Manasseh and is uniquely identified as the firstborn son of Joseph, born to him and Asenath in Egypt. His birth and lineage are significant within the context of Israel's history, especially as his descendants formed a large and influential tribe.
namesAndTitles: The name Manasseh means 'one that makes to forget,' a proper name not given directly by God. This meaning reflects the circumstances surrounding his birth as recorded in Genesis.
familyAndRelationships: Manasseh was the son of Joseph and Asenath, making him part of the patriarchal lineage that includes several ancestors and descendants. His father was Joseph, and he is noted as the father of Machir. His lineage includes numerous ancestors such as Pedahzur, Susi, Jair, Ephod, and others, and he had descendants like Ben-geber, indicating a well-documented family line within Scripture.
scriptureSignificance: Manasseh holds a crucial place in biblical history as the firstborn son of Joseph, whose tribe grew to become one of the most numerous and powerful among Israel. Although Manasseh was the firstborn, the greater blessing was given to his younger brother Ephraim, demonstrating God's sovereign will over customary birthrights. His descendants settled on both sides of the Jordan River, playing a vital role in the fulfillment of God's promises to Israel.
